moat_against: Copart — entrenched, higher-margin rival setting the bar in salvage
ROIC proxy only 7.6-7.8% in 2024-25 post-IAA (vs 25.4% pre-deal in 2022) — deal capital not yet earning its cost
Service revenue take rate fell 110bp to 20.0% in Q2 2026 — pricing/mix pressure, no proven pricing power now
Cyclical GTV (construction, transport, auto) and insurer-controlled salvage supply
Growth partly bought (BigIron $316.6M, Blackmon $17M in 2026) — goodwill keeps stacking
moat_for: Liquidity network effects — largest buyer/seller pool for used heavy equipment and transportation assets, 40+ auction sites
IAA's entrenched insurer relationships in salvage vehicles — a two-player market with Copart
Physical yard/site network and local permits that take years to replicate
Ancillary data/services (Rouse, SmartEquip, VeriTread) deepening seller lock-in
Trusted brands — Ritchie Bros. since 1958, IAA in salvage
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat: genuine liquidity network effects and scale as the largest used heavy-equipment marketplace plus IAA's entrenched insurer position in the two-player salvage market, a hard-to-replicate yard/site network, and ancillary data services — but measured returns cap it at 5: the ROIC proxy fell from 25.4% (FY2022, pre-IAA) to 4.6% (2023) and has recovered only to 7.8% (2024) / 7.6% (2025), below cost of capital on the post-deal capital base; operating margin is mid-teens (15.5% FY2025, 16.0% TTM; gross margin not filed in fundamentals.json); Copart is the stronger salvage rival; and the Q2 2026 service take rate fell 110bp to 20.0%, evidence against current pricing power.
name: RB Global, Inc
one_liner: Leading commercial-asset marketplace (Ritchie Bros. + IAA), moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $84.30 (weighted IRR 7.6%, IV@15% $32.32; even super bull is 11.7%); it clears 15% only near $32.
sector: Industrials / Business services — asset marketplaces & auctions
